newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says not about to enter wheat market.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says not about to enter wheat market.

text.p: The Egyptian government said on Thursday it had wheat stocks to last for the rest of this year and saw no immediate need to enter the wheat market.

"I have all my requirements covered till the end of the year. So we are not planning to enter unless there is something that makes us enter," said Samir Shakankiri, vice chairman of the state's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC).
Shakankiri, whose organisation is the biggest wheat importer in Egypt, told Reuters local farmers had already delivered 1.3 million tonnes of wheat to GASC and more was arriving.
"Then I have recently procured 600,000 tonnes from abroad and I have my strategic stocks -- I will not say how much they are but it is more than 1.1 million tonnes," he added.
